summary: Iter8 profile-editor / pin-round / friends-screen suite tested end-to-end. Backend: 9/10 pytest cases PASS. One CRITICAL backend spec failure: PATCH /api/auth/me with {"handicap": null} does NOT clear the field (handicap remains at prior value). This is a direct miss against the review spec 'Handicap can be set to null to clear.' Root cause identified — see rca_of_issue. All other backend behaviour matches spec: PATCH persists display_name/bio/home_course/handicap/avatar; oversized avatar (>800k b64) returns 413; POST /rounds/{id}/pin is owner-only (403 for non-owner, 404 for missing round); DELETE /users/me/pin clears; GET /users/{id} returns pinned_round (enriched or null), round_count=2, avg_score=80.5, courses_played=2, friends_count=2 for reese; stale pinned_round auto-clears on GET /users/{id} after the pinned round is deleted (no orphan pinned_round_id in response); GET /users/{id}/friends returns mutual-follow list with correct shape and sort (friends first, alphabetical). Frontend: verified via mobile Playwright at 390x844 — profile-name renders 'Reese Callahan · 8.4 HCP' inline; stat row shows only Rounds/Avg/Courses/Friends (no Handicap/Best cell); Friends stat tappable and opens /user/{me}/friends showing 'Your friends' title with Mutual friend badges and Follow/Following toggles; Edit pill opens Profile Editor with all 7 required testIDs (name/handicap/home/bio/pick-avatar/save/back); save persists and reflects immediately on profile; Post Detail for an owned round renders post-pin-toggle that flips 'Pin to profile' → 'Pinned' with green background; profile-pinned-round badge with 'Pinned round' header appears on the profile above 'Your rounds'; other user's profile (jordan) renders identical 4-stat row with tappable user-stat-friends → '/user/{id}/friends' rendering "Jordan's friends · 2 friends · 1 mutual with you" header; the viewer's own row shows a 'You' badge, other rows show 'Mutual friend' + Following. user-pinned-round hidden for jordan (no pin), rendered for reese when a round is pinned.

critical.issue: Cannot clear handicap by sending {"handicap": null}. Server drops None-valued fields via `updates = {k: v for k, v in data.dict().items() if v is not None}` (server.py:323). Spec requires null to clear. Frontend (app/profile/edit.tsx:79) already sends handicap:null when the field is empty, so users cannot actually remove their handicap via the Profile Editor.

integration_issues.issue: UI sends handicap:null but backend ignores it, so leaving the Handicap field blank and hitting Save appears to succeed but the handicap remains unchanged after the modal closes. User-visible defect once the backend fix is in place; frontend code is correct.

action_items: server.py:321-329 (update_me): stop dropping None values wholesale. Use `data.dict(exclude_unset=True)` (or model_dump(exclude_unset=True) if Pydantic v2) so fields that were explicitly sent as null pass through to `$set` and can clear the DB value. Alternatively special-case handicap: keep None-filter for other keys but always $set handicap when the key is present in the request body. Re-run test_iter8_profile.py::TestProfileEditor::test_patch_me_handicap_null_clears to verify.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:321-329 — using data.dict() (all fields defaulting to None) + `if v is not None` filter means PATCH semantics are effectively 'set-any-provided-non-null-value', not 'set-what-was-sent'. This silently swallows explicit null clears and could confuse other future clear-by-null use cases (bio='' still works because it's an empty string, not None, but handicap has no sentinel).

server.py:458-511 (get_user): correct stale-pin auto-clear via $unset when the referenced round no longer exists (verified). Friends_count and courses_played implementations look correct and match the seed expectations.

server.py:518-542 (get_user_friends): shape and sort verified (friends first, then alphabetical, viewer perspective is_following/is_friend/is_me). Consider projecting only the fields the client uses to keep the payload light, but not a bug.
server.py:545-558 (pin/unpin): 403 for non-owner and 404 for missing round both verified; no rate limit here but that's acceptable given the auth requirement.
frontend/app/profile/edit.tsx:79 — sends handicap:null which is the correct client behaviour. No change needed once the backend accepts nulls.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: /app/backend/server.py:323 uses `updates = {k: v for k, v in data.dict().items() if v is not None}`. Pydantic's `.dict()` on a model with `Optional[float] = None` returns all declared fields including keys the client never sent, all defaulted to None. The current filter drops both 'unset' fields and 'explicitly-set-to-null' fields identically, so there is no way to clear handicap. Reproduction: `curl -X PATCH .../api/auth/me -H 'Auth: Bearer <reese>' -d '{"handicap": null}'` → 200, but subsequent GET /api/auth/me still returns the previous handicap. Mitigation: switch to `data.dict(exclude_unset=True)` (Pydantic v1) or `data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` (v2). This preserves the current behaviour for unset fields while allowing explicit null to reach `$set`, which MongoDB will store as BSON null (and public_user()/enrich_round() already handle handicap=None correctly downstream).
